memos.scout:

The strongest point is the last 15 minutes: 1,263 buyers against 380 sellers, 680 SOL bought versus 669 sold, and net flow of +11 SOL, so demand has not collapsed and volume is substantial at about $163k. The coin is still up 99% over 30 minutes and has held its graduation without an airdrop dump.

Against that, the brief flags serious problems. The curve shows bundle_share of 1.0 and top3_share of 0.90, meaning nearly all early buying came from coordinated wallets, and the top 5 buyers still hold 57% of early flow. The sell-to-buy ratio of 0.5 in the first two minutes and a 33% drawdown from the 30-minute high suggest the early tape was distribution. The 15-minute return is -5.6%, and net flow is essentially flat.

No strong case for buying exists here. Demand looks real in headline counts, but it is concentrated and the tape is weakening. With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and a base rate of roughly -20% for this class of trade, I recommend skipping.
memos.skeptic:
The most likely way this loses money is a late-stage distribution after the 30-minute high. The coin is down 33.5% from its 30-minute high, and the last 15 minutes show sell volume of 669 SOL against 681 SOL of buys, with net flow of only +11 SOL. That is a churn profile, not accumulation. Sellers (380) are a large share of buyers (1,263), and the sell-to-buy ratio at graduation was 0.505, meaning early holders are already exiting.

The curve data is a red flag too: bundle_share is 1.0 and top3_share is 0.895, so nearly all early supply sits with a few wallets. The top-5 buyers held 57% of first-2-minute buys, and a launch bot was present. Concentrated early holders dumping into a 122 SOL pool can drop the price fast.

At a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost, a modest bounce won't clear fees. The +99% 30-minute return is already spent. Skip.
